## What this document does not claim

**A mapping is not a verification, and this document claims no level.** A verification level attaches to a verification *of an application* performed by an assessor against that application; a template cannot hold one and a generator cannot confer one. This map states which live control in the tree bears on each requirement, how much of it that control reaches, and what is left — so an assessor starts from an honest ledger and a consumer never mistakes a template for a verification. It never says the generated application is ASVS Level 1, 2 or 3, MASVS-verified, or CRA-conformant, and `tools/check-conformance-map.mjs` reds any sentence in the register that does.

**The CRA rows carry a shelf life.** CRA conformity is a manufacturer’s legal act — Annex I obligations, a conformity assessment, a declaration, CE marking — that no code tree performs, and no harmonised standard for the CRA had been cited in the Official Journal as of 2026-08-16 — the register records: “none cited in the Official Journal as of the verified date; ETSI’s CRA ENs were in approval — re-verify per the calendar row conformance-cra-hens-citation”. The Annex I rows are mapped against the regulation’s text directly and must be re-read when a harmonised standard is cited.

**Module rows are conditional.** 8 row(s) rest on an opt-in module (`module` set in the register) and are graded on the assumption that the module is enabled; on a tree without it the row is CONDITIONAL, judged for liveness only where the module’s `docs/modules/<name>/README.md` marker exists, and its control may not run here at all.

**Organisation-boundary rows are enumerated, never graded up.** 39 row(s) name something only the operating organisation can meet (policies, processes, notifications, contracts); the register may not grade them `covered` or `partial`, and this document lists them so nobody mistakes the tree’s silence for the operator’s compliance.

**Grades are conservative by rule.** Absence of a surface is never coverage; where two grades are defensible the lower is taken; `covered` may not rest on documentation alone; and `not-covered` is not a failure the gate reds on — it is the honest statement of what would be needed.

## Unmapped chain steps

Steps that run on every validate and are named as no row’s control, each with its recorded reason.

- `format` — Source formatting (biome) has no subject in ASVS, MASVS or CRA Annex I — it is the harness’s own consistency floor, not an application security requirement.
- `wiring` — Hook/settings/lockfile wiring is the harness’s self-integrity check — that ITS enforcement is installed — and no requirement in the three standards asks an application to prove its development harness is wired.
- `suppressions` — The inline-suppression census governs how the enforcement layer may be silenced; it is a control ON the controls, and none of the standards enumerates it as an application requirement.
- `provenance` — Citation discipline on decision sites is a development-process control; CRA Annex I Part II asks for vulnerability handling and documentation, not for cited authorities on decision lines, and ASVS/MASVS do not ask for it at all.
- `boundaries` — Package-layering and export-wall closure is architectural hygiene (verticals ⊥ verticals, the reversibility wall); ASVS 5.0 dropped its architecture chapter and no remaining row demands module boundaries.
- `native-deps` — The reviewed native-module allowlist is Expo build hygiene; MASVS-CODE speaks to third-party components generally and is mapped through the dependency lanes, not through this allowlist.
- `prompts` — Prompt-file hash locking governs LLM prompt provenance — no row in the three standards addresses it.
- `licenses` — Licence compliance is a legal obligation outside all three security standards.
- `types-drift` — Freshness of the generated Supabase type mirror is a correctness control with no security-requirement subject.
- `migrations` — Append-only migration discipline and the DML/ADR markers are change-management hygiene; the schema controls that DO map (RLS, grants, audit) are claimed by schema-rls and tenancy, and claiming this step too would count one artefact twice.
- `parity` — Web/mobile feature parity has no security-requirement subject.
- `build` — That the tree compiles is a precondition of every other control, not a requirement any standard states.
- `styleguide` — Design-token discipline has no security-requirement subject.
- `perf-budget` — Bundle and interaction budgets have no security-requirement subject; the effect-cleanup leak scan is availability hygiene, not a standard’s row.
- `e2e` — The e2e step asserts spec PRESENCE for routes; the security-bearing e2e specs themselves are claimed by the web-e2e lane rows.
- `docs-sync` — docs-sync is the step that RUNS the two conformance registers and the documentation-drift closures; it is the judge of this map, so it may not be named as evidence inside it.
- `diff-coverage` — Per-file coverage floors are a test-quality control with no security-requirement subject; ASVS 5.0 carries no testing chapter.
- `duplication` — Token-clone detection has no security-requirement subject.
- `i18n` — The catalog-key rule and the Intl ban have no security-requirement subject.
- `test-quality` — Assertion-free/focused/disabled test detection is a test-quality control with no security-requirement subject.
- `mobile-perf` — Maestro-flow and startup-budget closure has no security-requirement subject.
